Vancouver, B.C. – TheNewswire - September 09, 2026 - Belmont Resources Inc. (TSX-V: BEA) (FSE: L3L2) ("Belmont" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the appointment of Ken Wheatley, P.Geol., M.Sc., as Senior Geological Advisor to the Company’s 100%-owned Crackingstone Uranium–REE Project, located within the historic Beaverlodge uranium district near Uranium City, Saskatchewan.

Crackingstone is a fault-hosted, Beaverlodge-model uranium project covering approximately 4 kilometres of the Black Bay Shear Zone and hosting four past-producing uranium mines. The Property is strategically located approximately 6 kilometres west of Uranium City, Saskatchewan. Its close proximity to the historic uranium mining centre provides important logistical advantages, including access to existing infrastructure, transportation and local services that can support exploration activities and future development. The property is drill-permitted.

Figure 1: Location map of the Crackingstone Property relative to Uranium City, Saskatchewan.

Mr. Wheatley brings over four decades of uranium exploration experience in the Athabasca Basin, most recently as Vice President, Exploration with Forum Energy Metals Corp. (2007–2023), and previously as District Geologist, East Athabasca, with AREVA Resources Canada Inc. (1998–2007). His earlier career included senior technical roles with Uranerz Exploration and Mining Ltd., TOTAL Minatco Ltee./Ltd., and Amok Ltee./Ltd., during which he was involved in the discovery and delineation of several major Athabasca Basin uranium deposits, including Midwest A, Maybelle River, the Sue deposits, and the Dominique Janine deposits at Cluff Lake. He holds an M.Sc. (1985) from the University of Saskatchewan and a B.Sc. (1980) from Laurentian University, and is a registered member of APEGS and NAPEG.

"Ken’s direct experience with the structural and alteration systems that control uranium mineralization throughout the Athabasca Basin makes him an ideal advisor as we advance Crackingstone," said George Sookochoff, Chairman of Belmont Resources Inc. "His track record of discovery at Key Lake, McClean/Sue, Midwest, and Northwest Athabasca speaks for itself, and we look forward to his guidance as we finalize our upcoming exploration and drilling program at Crackingstone. The Crackingstone Uranium Project has an enormous amount of historical exploration data, and we have been using AI to compile that data and delineate high-quality targets. Ken is now working with us, and combining his decades of hands-on uranium exploration experience with AI’s ability to rapidly synthesize and cross-reference decades of historic drilling, geophysics, and geochemistry, has already sharpened our view of where the next holes should go."

As previously disclosed in the Company’s news release dated February 3, 2026, Belmont's re-assaying of selected intervals of historic drill core at Crackingstone identified multiple intervals exhibiting elevated uranium and rare earth element (REE) concentrations, including several zones where uranium and REE enrichment occur together. Mr. Wheatley is now working with the Company to incorporate this uranium–REE potential, together with the Project’s structural and geophysical data, into the design of the next phase of exploration and drilling at Crackingstone.

About Belmont Resources Inc.
